meta.title: Too Much Change
meta.textType: story: a school shop and a mistake that nobody names

paragraphs: At twelve o'clock on Tuesday, February second, Leo and Mia stood at the school shop window. A price board hung beside the window. A pencil cost ten baht, a ruler cost fifteen baht, and a notebook cost twenty-five baht. A woman in a green apron stood behind the window. That morning, Teacher Kim gave Leo a hundred-baht note and a short list. "The math exam is on Friday," she said. "We use pencils instead of pens in the exam," she said, "so buy two pencils, a ruler, and a notebook." "Count the change exactly, and do not spend it on sweets, because there is no extra money." Mia went with Leo because she added numbers fast. "Counting is not my favorite thing," said Leo.

Leo took the note out of his pocket and held it in one hand. In the other hand, he held the list. Mia counted on her fingers, and her lips moved. "Twenty baht for two pencils, plus fifteen baht for the ruler, plus twenty-five baht for the notebook," she whispered. "The total is sixty baht." Other shoppers waited in a line behind them, so Leo hurried. "Sixty baht, please," said the woman. Leo gave her the note. She put the pencils, the ruler, and the notebook in Mia's arms. Then she put one twenty-baht note and three ten-baht coins in Leo's hand. "Is that the right change?" asked Mia. "Wait, I want to count it again," said Leo. He counted the money twice, and then he looked at Mia.

Leo walked back to the window with one ten-baht coin in his hand. Mia followed him with the pencils, the ruler, and the notebook in her arms. "Excuse me," said Leo, and he held out the coin. The woman looked at the coin. She looked at Leo, and then she looked at Mia. Nobody spoke for a moment. Then the woman laughed and took the coin. "Next shopper, please," she said.
Mia smiled all the way to the classroom. Leo walked beside her with his hands in his pockets.

In the classroom, Leo gave the change to Teacher Kim, and she counted it. "One twenty-baht note and two ten-baht coins," she said. "That is exactly forty baht." "Who counted the change?" she asked. "Leo did, twice," said Mia. "Counting twice takes only a minute," said Leo. "That is a good rule for an exam, too," said Teacher Kim.
text.summary: Teacher Kim sends Leo and Mia to the school shop with a list and a hundred-baht note. The woman at the window gives Leo too much change, and Leo counts it again and takes one coin back.
